name: USA
lead: The United States stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific. It has 50 states, with mountains, deserts, and tropical islands. Americans invented the lightbulb, the aeroplane, and the internet. About 340 million people live there.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The USA has six time zones and almost every climate. The Rocky Mountains split the west.
Alaska has glaciers and the continent's tallest peak. Hawaii lies 3,800 km out in the Pacific. The Grand Canyon, a huge deep valley, makes its own weather.
animals: The bald eagle has been the national symbol since 1782. Bison once numbered 60 million on the Great Plains. Hunters nearly wiped them out.
Monarch butterflies fly 4,000 km each autumn to Mexican forests. Wolves returned to Yellowstone National Park in 1995. They kept elk moving and changed the course of rivers.
culture: American culture is a remix. Jazz began in New Orleans. Hip-hop began in New York. Billions of people watch Hollywood films.
New York has pizza, Texas has barbecue, and Louisiana has gumbo (a thick stew). The USA has about 17,000 public libraries, more than McDonald's restaurants.
history: American Indians lived here for 15,000 years before Europeans came. In 1776, Britain's 13 colonies (lands it ruled overseas) declared independence. They won the Revolutionary War and launched the first modern democracy.
It fought a Civil War (1861–65) to end slavery. After the Cold War (a rivalry with the Soviet Union) ended in 1991, it was the world's only top power.
wows: The USA has over 1,200 tornadoes a year, more than any other country.
Alaska is closer to Russia than to the other mainland states, just 88 km of sea away.
The Library of Congress, the world's largest library, holds over 175 million items.
Yellowstone Park sits on a supervolcano. Its magma (melted rock) chamber is as big as Los Angeles.
Americans eat about 3 billion pizzas every year.
Laid end to end, US highways between states could circle Earth's equator nearly twice.
More Nobel Prize winners came from the USA than any other country, over 400.

myths.myth: The Statue of Liberty was made in America
myths.fact: France built it as a gift in 1886. It crossed the ocean in 350 pieces.

myths.myth: Lightning never strikes the same place twice
myths.fact: It often does. The Empire State Building gets hit about 20 times a year.
